newsitem.title: USA: U.S. passenger jet lands at wrong airport.
newsitem.headline: U.S. passenger jet lands at wrong airport.

text.p: A Continental Airlines jet en route from Houston to Corpus Christi, Texas landed at the wrong airport, an airline spokesman said on Monday.

The Boeing 737-500 carrying 54 passengers touched down on Sunday at a nearly abandoned Second World War-era airfield four miles (6.4 kilometres) from its intended destination, Corpus Corpus International Airport.
Continental spokesman Dave Messing said it was not clear why the jet landed at the wrong place, but both the airline and the Federal Aviation Administration were investigating.
"We're reviewing the circumstances to see how it occurred. Pending the conclusion of our review, we really don't have further details to convey to you," Messing said.
He said the crew piloting the jet would be "off of active duty" until the review was completed.
Messing said the jet suffered no damage and there were no injuries, although passengers described the landing as a hard one. They were bused to Corpus Christi International airport.
The pilots were replaced by a new crew who flew the jet back to Houston, where Continental is based.
The airfield where the flight landed was a naval air station during the Second World War. It is used now as a place for pilots in training to practice their takeoffs and landings.
